subject: Running multiple parallel instances of INLA on a server

messages.author: 87e020c3fd9325fa
messages.subject: Running multiple parallel instances of INLA on a server
parts:
Hi all,

I have been having some problems trying to get multiple instances of the same INLA model running in parallel. I am unsure if it is because I am using a lot of memory (43Gb) or if it is because the server cannot run multiple instances of INLA.  

The model I amusing is a poisson approximation to the multinomial distribution, with the following formula:


form=value~ -1 + 

      f(GISID, model="iid", hyper = list(prec = list( initial = log(0.000001), fixed = TRUE))) +

    f(Cat, model="iid", constr = TRUE, hyper = list(prec = list(initial = log(0.001), fixed = TRUE)))   + (Dummy covariates)


Here is my inla() call:

out=inla(form=form, family = "poisson", E=TOT_POP, data = prddat,

          control.inla = list( strategy = "laplace", int.strategy = "eb"),

          control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE), 

          control.compute=list(dic=FALSE, config=TRUE), verbose=FALSE)


The model seems to run ok.  but the error comes when I do inla.posterior.sample() on the output

   xx=inla.posterior.sample(nsample, out)

It seems as though the model runs fine so long as I only run single instances of the model in a for loop.  As soon as I initiate a new model (even as a separate job on the server) the first job crashes with an error message like this:

Error in inla.collect.results(results.dir, control.results = cont.results,  : 

  This is not a directory:  /tmp/RtmpXycjGv/file3db83d792448/results.files 

Error in inla.posterior.sample(nsample, out) : 

  You need an inla-object computed with option 'control.compute=list(config = TRUE)'.

Calls: run_MN_SNOW -> inla.posterior.sample

Execution halted

The funny thing is that it will run for 3-4 iterations,  then crash with the above message.  

I have also tried with a number of 'default' settings in control.inla and control.compute.

Any suggestions would be vary helpful

Many thanks,

Tom

Tom,

could you check that the inla-program on the server and your installed
R-INLA is of the same version? There have been some changes recently,
which will cause a crash if they're out of sync.

Otherwise, the strategy="laplace" might be very costly... Your use of
memory is certainly an issue which might cause a problem, if the program
request an ammount and does not get it. Some of the external libs does
not give an appropriate error message in this case.

to test that the concept is working, try with
